newsitem.title: USA: August Brent crude sinks in late US paper trading.
newsitem.headline: August Brent crude sinks in late US paper trading.

text.p: North Sea Brent crude oil sank in late U.S. paper trading on Wednesday, with a European player attributed with all of the selling, traders said.
Six partial August cargoes switched hands a total of 850 times, once at $18.78, twice at $18.80, twice at $18.83 and once at $18.84 a barrel.
London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) settled at $18.91 a barrel for the August contract. July settled at $18.71.
Intermonth spreads were subdued. June/July Brent was talked at minus 30/25 cents a barrel. July/August was pegged at minus 19/17, while August/September was around minus 15/13 a barrel.
